Option 2: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
--- END OF PROVIDED PORTION ---

Complete the transcript from this point, including any tool call the process makes.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it into smaller, similar subproblems. Each recursive call works on a simpler or smaller version of the original problem. To avoid an infinite loop, every recursive function needs a base case: a condition where it stops calling itself and returns a result directly. You can think of it like going down a staircase step by step, and the base case is when you reach the bottom and stop.
